tasks.spec:
You are fixing ONE parsing assumption in ONE Python file. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/guest_assets.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                    (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## What was measured against the live mailbox

This module resolves a guest's bio, contact details and headshot, preferring what the guest sent over anything generated. It passed its check and was then run against the real Gmail thread it was written for. The headshot and the contacts came back correctly. The bio came back as a gap, and on a second run with the real line endings it came back as the RESEARCHED description instead of the guest's own paragraph:

    sent: "Mike Guelcher, MBA, CEPA is a Certified Exit Planning Advisor through the Exit Planning Institute and managing partner and co-founder of Prism Consulting Partners..."
    back: "Consultant/Exit Planning Advisor + former industry and M&A executive"

That second string is a generated label. Substituting it for his own words is precisely the defect this module exists to prevent — it is what the prep document did, and it is what would have been read on air.

## The cause, measured not guessed

The live message body is CRLF-delimited. Paragraph breaks are `\r\n\r\n`, not `\n\n`. The parsing splits paragraphs on `\n\n`, so the entire message is one blob, the bio cannot be isolated, and the code falls through to the next source in the authority order.

The raw bytes, from the live message:

    "...?viewAsMember=true\r\n\r\nHere's a quick bio.  If you'd like something different or condensed, please let me know.  The sentences are a bit lengthy : - ) \r\n\r\nMike Guelcher, MBA, CEPA is a Certified Exit Planning Advisor..."

Note also the DOUBLE SPACE after each full stop. Real people write like this and the parsing must not assume single spaces.

## The fix

Normalise line endings at the point the message text enters the module: convert `\r\n` and a lone `\r` to `\n` before any splitting, matching or offset arithmetic. Do it once, in one place, so no later change can reintroduce the assumption. Be similarly tolerant of runs of spaces where you match cue phrases.

Do NOT normalise the bio VALUE you return. The guest's words are returned exactly as he wrote them — his double spaces, his smiley, his long sentence. Normalisation is for finding the text, never for rewriting it. If you strip or reflow what you return, the check fails on verbatim comparison, and rightly.

## What must NOT change

  * the authority order: what the guest sent beats research, which beats the web;
  * `exact` is true only for what the guest himself supplied;
  * an asset no source has is a named gap, never an empty string and never invented;
  * one unreadable source degrades only itself and leaves a coverage trace;
  * no network, no filesystem, no new imports beyond the standard library already used.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u21_guest_assets_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

Its fixture now delivers the message with CRLF endings and double spaces, exactly as Gmail returns it. It currently fails with bio_not_verbatim and guest_bio_not_marked_exact.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' name another message shape that could still defeat the bio extraction. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Drives the resolver with the guest's message in the exact shape Gmail returns it — CRLF paragraph breaks and double spaces after full stops — and requires his bio back byte-for-byte and marked as his, rather than the generated label the code currently falls through to. The fallback, gap, exactness and degraded-source assertions all still execute, so the fix cannot be bought by loosening the authority order.
